findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_workers.py (diff ~L357 and offer_order L322-324). `for pr in sorted(list_prs(), key=offer_order(kinds))` runs before the `only_prs`/`exclude_prs` `continue`. The runner's `--exclude-pr` and `--pr` (candidate_prs only_prs path, which returns a closed unmerged PR via pulls/N) both reach the sort. Before this change, such PRs were skipped or tolerated. The failure also bypasses the per-PR try/except that names and skips a bad PR. A lazy stub whose Issues `pull_request.merged_at` is null fails the same way.
findings.summary: work_next sorts the whole listing with offer_order before applying only_prs/exclude_prs, and offer_order raises WorkerError for any non-open PR without merged_at. One such PR in the listing therefore aborts the run, even when it is excluded or not targeted.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/github_read_cache.py: `_page` returns `entry["body"]` and `parsed`, both of which now live in `_memo`. The `_load` docstring only says "Callers never mutate the result", and nothing enforces it. `_page` still recomputes `_digest(entry["body"])` on every read, but the memo was populated before that check, so a mutated body would be seen as corrupt. The cost of that per-read digest also remains and is not discussed in the design.
findings.summary: The process-wide memo hands out the same parsed objects to every caller, and _store memoizes the very `parsed` object it also returns. A caller that mutates a result from get_json/get_pages silently corrupts later reads in that process. Digest validation happens only on load, so the corruption is never detected.
